ablations.prompt: Explain inflation to a 10-year-old. Use exactly 3 bullet points.

runs.answer:
- Inflation means prices go up over time. A candy bar that cost 50 cents when your grandparents were kids might cost a dollar or more today.

- It happens because money gets a little less powerful. If there is more money around chasing the same toys, snacks, and houses, sellers can charge more for them.

- A little inflation is normal and healthy, like your height going up slowly each year. Too much happening too fast is a problem, because then your allowance buys less and less.

- Inflation is when prices slowly go up over time, so the same amount of money buys fewer things than it used to. A candy bar that cost 50 cents when your grandparents were kids might cost a dollar or more today.

- Think of your allowance: if you save $10 but the price of your favorite toys goes up every year, your $10 can buy less and less. That's inflation shrinking what your money can do.

- Grown-ups who run the economy, like the central bank, try to keep inflation at a steady, gentle pace, because if prices go up too fast or fall too much, it can make it hard for families and businesses to plan.
